The petition no. 240/MP/2023 was filed on 31.07.2023 and listed for hearing on 19.01.2024. whereas, petition no. 302/MP/2023 was filed on 14.09.2023 and listed for hearing on 14.02.2024. After hearing the parties' submissions, the Commission admitted the petitions. The petitions were listed on 03.07.2025. During the course of the hearing, the Petitioner and KSEBL made detailed submissions and concluded their respective arguments. The Commission permitted the parties to file their written submissions. Accordingly, the matters were reserved for orders. binding on both parties in case of ‘Change in Law.’ Further, as per Clause 1.1(5) of the mutually agreed PPA, the Appropriate Commission shall mean the _Kerala State Electricity Regulatory Commission_ . Thus, as per the PPA, the appropriate Forum to deal with any claim of Change in Law is KSERC. However, TPSL has never raised these issues before KSERC. On this ground alone, the present Petition is not maintainable and deserves to be dismissed at the threshold itself. # ** Submission by Additional Affidavit dated 01.07.2025 by the Petitioner: ** 13. On the basis of the submissions of the contracting parties, the following issues arise for adjudication: **_ Issue No. III: _** _Whether the Petitioner is entitled to carrying cost/interest towards compensation for the Change in Law?_ 15. We observe that the facts relating to maintainability/jurisdiction are the same in petition no. 302/MP/2024 and petition no. 240/MP/2023. The Commission has already decided the issue vide its earlier order dated 20.02.2025 in Petition No. 240/MP/2023, wherein it was held as under: _22. ..We note that it is a well-settled principle of law that the parties, by their agreement, can neither confer jurisdiction upon a forum that does not have the jurisdiction under the law nor can the parties, by their agreement, oust the jurisdiction of the forum vested under the law._ _“ .where the parties to a contract agreed to submit the disputes arising from it to a particular jurisdiction which would otherwise also be a proper jurisdiction under the law their agreement to the extent they agreed not to submit to other jurisdictions cannot be said to be void as against public policy. If on the other hand the jurisdiction they agreed to submit to would not otherwise be proper jurisdiction to decide disputes arising out of the contract it must be declared void being against public policy.”_ _“By a long series of decisions it has been held that where two Courts or more have under the CPC jurisdiction to try a suit or proceeding an agreement between the parties that the dispute between them shall be tried in any one of such Courts is not contrary to public policy and in no way contravenes Section 28 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872. Therefore, if on the facts of a given case more than one Court has jurisdiction, parties by their consent may limit the jurisdiction to one of the two Courts. But by an agreement parties cannot confer jurisdiction to a Court which otherwise does not have jurisdiction to deal with a matter.”_ _25. In the light of the above position of law, we are of the view that merely because the PPA mentions adjudication of the dispute in a specific manner, it cannot oust the jurisdiction of this Commission, which flows from the provisions of the Act. Hence, we hold that adjudication involving the parties will be governed by this Commission under Section 79 (1)(f), read with Section 79(1)(b) of the Act._ _26._ **_ In view of the above discussion we find and hold that only this Commission has the jurisdiction. The petitions are admitted accordingly. _** _It is clarified that this_ _Order is limited to the determination of issues of the jurisdiction of this Commission and we have not expressed any view on the merit of the issues raised in the Petition. The parties shall complete pleadings in the matter within four weeks of the issue of this order. No further extension of time for completion of pleadings shall be permitted.”_ _12.2.2 The decision of the appropriate Commission shall be final and governing on both the Parties._ **_Whether the Petitioner is entitled to carrying cost/interest towards compensation for the Change in Law?_** _12.2.2 The decision of the appropriate Commission shall be final and governing on both the Parties._ _84. It is in the above context that we accept that the regulatory powers of the Central Commission ought to have been properly exercised to do complete justice to the claims for compensation, it having been denied by depriving the SPPDs of their legitimate expectation of relief vis-à-vis the burden of carrying cost as well, rendering the dispensation partially unfair._ _“Pending further orders, the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC) shall comply with the directions issued in paragraph 109 of the impugned order dated 15 September 2022 of the Appellate Tribunal for Electricity. However, the final order of the CERC shall not be enforced pending further orders.”_ - f) The directions issued in this Order so far as they relate to compensation for the period post Commercial Operation Date of the projects in question as also towards carrying cost (pre-COD & post-COD) shall not be enforced and shall be subject to further orders of the Hon’ble Supreme Court in Civil Appeal No. 8880/2022 in _Telangana Northern_
